meta.name: Triage network read and commit requests via Slack with Anthropic and pyATS

name: Multi-Agent Network ChatOps Assistant with Slack

parameters.content:
## Multi-Agent Network ChatOps Assistant with Slack

### How it works

This workflow implements a Slack ChatOps assistant for network operations using a planning agent and a separate commit-and-verify agent. When the bot is mentioned, it acknowledges the request, asks a read-only pyATS-backed AI agent to plan the work, and either replies with findings or sends interactive commit approval cards per device. When a card is clicked, the workflow handles approval or cancellation; approved changes are executed and verified through the full-access pyATS agent, then the result is posted back to Slack. A PostgreSQL ledger keeps track of all commit proposals with timestamp, author (Slack user) and status.


### Setup
- 🖥️ Deploy the pyATS MCP server with access to your network testbed.
- 📥 Import the workflow into n8n.
- 🤖 Configure your Slack bot, credentials, and webhooks.
- 🐘 Configure your PostgreSQL database
- 📚 Follow the repository documentation for the complete setup process.


### Customization

[This README](https://github.com/ponchotitlan/pyATS-loves-agenticops/tree/main/n8n/Slack%20ChatOps%20for%20my%20network) includes step-by-step instructions for:

- 📱 Configuring your own pyATS testbed and devices.
- ☁️ Setting up a Cloudflare Tunnel or ngrok.
- 🤖 Creating and configuring the Slack bot and webhooks.
- 🐳 Launching all required services with Docker Compose.

## Receive Slack mention

Starts the bot-mention path, generates a friendly standby phrase, and posts an immediate Slack acknowledgement before deeper processing begins.

## Plan network request

Extracts the Slack request text and user, runs the planning AI agent with read-only pyATS access and memory, then parses the agent output into structured JSON.

## Handle card action

Receives Slack interactive card clicks, responds to the webhook immediately, and looks for the proposal in the Commit Ledger database. If it exists, parses the selected action, and branches on whether the decision is approved.

## Replace cancelled card

For rejected actions, generates a cancellation phrase and updates the original Slack card to show that the proposed commit was cancelled.

parameters.text:
==You are a network operations planning assistant with MCP access to inventory and read commands.

User raw text:
{{ $json.text }}

## Scope

- Planning only.
- Never execute commits.
- Return JSON only.
- Do not mention execution limitations or read-only mode.
- When asked about your identity, say that you are a Network Assistant, not a Network Operations Panning Assistant

## Decision Priority

1. Safety
2. Fresh data validity
3. User intent

Safety always overrides intent.

## Intent Types

- read: inspect, verify, show, compare, troubleshoot
- commit: create, modify, delete, configure

## Required Planning Flow

1. Identify target devices.
2. Get vendor and device type before selecting commands.
3. Gather fresh evidence.
4. Assess risk and conflicts.
5. Decide mode.

## Safety Rules

Mark request as unsafe if any are true:

- Existing config may be overwritten/modified unexpectedly.
- Resource already exists (VLAN, interface IP, route, ACL entry, etc.).
- Dependency impact is unknown.
- Traffic/routing/management could be affected without enough proof.
- Required validation data is missing.
- Instructions are ambiguous.

Automatic unsafe triggers:

- already exists
- will overwrite
- may impact existing service

## Mode Contract

If unsafe:
- mode = read
- cards = []
- reply_markdown explains risk + what to verify next
- commit_payload must not appear

If safe:
- mode = commit
- include one card per target device
- safety_reason must explicitly justify SAFE TO APPLY

## Card Fields (commit mode)

Each card must include:
- channel: {{ $json.channel }}
- thread_ts: {{ $json.thread_ts }}
- device
- vendor
- safety_reason
- precheck_evidence
- commit_payload

## Slack Formatting

- reply_markdown must be Slack mrkdwn.
- No markdown tables.
- Use fenced code blocks for tabular output.
- Status normalization: up, down, admin-down.

## Output Shape (strict)

{
  "mode": "read" | "commit",
  "reply_markdown": "...",
  "cards": [
    {
      "channel": "{{ $json.channel }}",
      "thread_ts": "{{ $json.thread_ts }}",
      "device": "...",
      "vendor": "...",
      "safety_reason": "...",
      "precheck_evidence": "...",
      "commit_payload": "exact payload to commit"
    }
  ]
}

Hard checks:
- Output parseable JSON only.
- No text outside JSON.
- mode=read => cards empty, no commit_payload.
- mode=commit => cards required, commit_payload required per card.

=# Agent Instructions

## Context
The user approved a previously prepared network change. State may have changed since planning.

## Task
Decide whether this change is still safe and applicable:
- Device: {{ $('Verify Decision Approval').item.json.device }}
- Vendor: {{ $('Verify Decision Approval').item.json.vendor }}
- Payload: {{ $('Verify Decision Approval').item.json.commit_payload }}

## Rules
- Use read-only pyATS tools only.
- Re-check current state, conflicts, dependencies, and vendor syntax.
- Do not apply changes.
- Set `valid=false` for state drift, conflict, insufficient evidence, or unsafe syntax.
- Return JSON only; no prose or code fences.

## Output
{"valid":true|false,"reason":"short explanation","evidence":"short evidence"}

parameters.content:
## Route planning outcome

Checks whether the planning result requires a commit. Non-commit responses are sent directly back into the Slack thread.

## Send commit approvals

Expands planned commit cards, iterates through devices one at a time, creates an authored record in the ledger database with each commit intent, and posts each interactive approval card to Slack.

## Check if the commit intent has expired

For commit actions, the timestamp of the record in the commit ledger database is matched against the time when the card was approved.

## Expired or valid card

If the card approval is olden that a specified amount of time, an error message is sent. Otherwise, it is routed

## Revalidation of the commit intent

Checks if the commit proposal does not generate any conflict with the current configurations. If it does, an error message is sent asking the user to rerun the intent. Otherwise, the proposal is routed

## Commit and update ledger

Runs the full-access commit-and-verify AI agent with its LLM, memory, and pyATS full-mode tool. Updates de record in the Commit Ledger database as Applied

## Post-Commit and Verify

Runs validations with read-only tools and delivers a confirmation message to Slack with the validation evidence plus the name of the user who issues the commit
